4.1 & Formal Definition of the Derivative & Compute derivatives from the difference-quotient limit; interpret as tangent slope / instantaneous rate. & \diffH \\
4.2.1 & Interpreting the Derivative & Interpret derivative values in context (velocity, reaction rate, growth rate). & \diffM \\
4.2.2 & Differentiability and Continuity & Explain the relationship between differentiability and continuity; find points of non-differentiability. & \diffM \\
4.3 & Power Rule and Basic Rules & Differentiate polynomials and power functions using the power, sum, and constant-multiple rules. & \diffL \\
4.4.1 & The Product Rule & Differentiate products of functions. & \diffM \\
4.4.2 & The Quotient Rule & Differentiate quotients, including rational and power functions. & \diffM \\
4.5.1 & The Chain Rule & Differentiate composite functions. & \diffH \\
4.5.2 & Proof of the Chain Rule & Follow a rigorous justification of the chain rule. & \diffM \\
4.6.1 & Implicit Differentiation & Differentiate implicitly defined relations to find $dy/dx$. & \diffH \\
4.6.2 & Related Rates & Set up and solve related-rates problems by differentiating a relation between time-dependent quantities. & \diffH \\
4.7 & Higher Derivatives & Compute second and higher derivatives; interpret their meaning. & \diffL \\
4.8 & Derivatives of Trigonometric Functions & Differentiate sine, cosine, tangent, and their combinations. & \diffM \\
4.9 & Derivatives of Exponential Functions & Differentiate $e^{x}$, $a^{x}$, and exponential growth/decay models. & \diffM \\
4.10.1 & Derivatives of Inverse Functions & Differentiate an inverse function using the inverse function theorem. & \diffM \\
4.10.2 & Derivative of the Logarithmic Function & Differentiate $\ln x$ and general logarithms. & \diffM \\
4.10.3\opt & Logarithmic Differentiation & Use logarithmic differentiation for products/quotients/powers of functions. & \diffM \\

\MajorTopics
\begin{itemize}
\item Functions of two or more variables: definitions, surface plots, heat maps, contour plots
\item * Limits and continuity (informal and formal definitions)
\item Partial derivatives (two and more variables; higher-order)
\item Tangent planes, differentiability, and linearization (scalar and vector-valued functions)
\item * The chain rule and implicit differentiation for functions of two variables
\item * Directional derivatives and gradient vectors
\item * Maximization and minimization: local and global extrema, extrema with constraints, least-squares data fitting
\item * Diffusion
\item * Systems of recurrence equations: a biological example, equilibria and stability (linear and nonlinear)
\end{itemize}
\KeyConcepts
Multivariable functions and their graphical representations (surfaces,
heat maps, contour/level curves); partial derivatives; tangent planes and
linearization; the multivariable chain rule; the gradient vector and
directional derivatives; critical-point classification; Lagrange
multipliers; least-squares regression; equilibria and stability of systems
of recurrence equations.
\LearnObj
\begin{enumerate}
\item Represent and interpret functions of two or more variables using surface, heat-map, and contour-plot representations.
\item Compute partial and higher-order partial derivatives.
\item Find the tangent plane to a surface and use linearization to approximate function values.
\item * Apply the multivariable chain rule and implicit differentiation.
\item * Compute directional derivatives and gradients, and interpret the gradient as the direction of steepest ascent.
\item * Find local, global, and constrained extrema (via Lagrange multipliers), and perform least-squares data fitting.
\item * Analyze equilibria and stability in systems of recurrence equations.
\end{enumerate}
\PreReq Single-variable differentiation and optimization (Chapters 4--5); vectors and matrices (Chapter 9).

\addcontentsline{toc}{subsection}{3.1 Calculus I}
\begin{longtable}{@{}p{0.10\textwidth}p{0.85\textwidth}@{}}
\toprule
\textbf{Week} & \textbf{Topics} \\
\midrule
\endhead
1 & Ch.\ 1.1--1.2 --- Diagnostic test; preliminaries (real numbers, lines, circles, trig, exponentials/logs, complex numbers) \\
2 & Ch.\ 1.3--1.4 --- Elementary functions; graphing and transformations \\
3 & Ch.\ 2.1--2.2 --- Discrete exponential growth; sequences and limits \\
4 & Ch.\ 2.3 --- Modeling with recurrence equations; Module A review \\
5 & \textbf{Exam 1}; Ch.\ 3.1 --- Limits \\
6 & Ch.\ 3.2--3.4 --- Continuity, limits at infinity, trigonometric limits \\
7 & Ch.\ 3.5 --- IVT and bisection; Ch.\ 4.1 --- Definition of the derivative \\
8 & Ch.\ 4.2--4.5 --- Differentiation rules through the chain rule \\
9 & \textbf{Exam 2}; Ch.\ 4.6--4.7 --- Implicit differentiation, related rates, higher derivatives \\
10 & Ch.\ 4.8--4.11 --- Derivatives of trig/exponential/log/inverse functions; linear approximation \\
11 & Ch.\ 5.1--5.3 --- Extrema, the MVT, monotonicity and concavity \\
12 & Ch.\ 5.4--5.6 --- Optimization, L'Hopital's Rule, curve sketching \\
13 & \textbf{Exam 3}; Ch.\ 5.10 --- Antiderivatives; Ch.\ 6.1 --- The definite integral \\
14 & Ch.\ 6.2--6.3 --- The Fundamental Theorem of Calculus and applications \\
15 & Review and \textbf{Final Exam} \\
\bottomrule
\end{longtable}

By the end of the course, a successful student will be able to:
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textbf{SLO\arabic*.}, leftmargin=2.6em]
\item \textbf{Model discrete and continuous change.} Translate a verbal description of a
      biological or social process into a recurrence equation, a limit statement, a
      derivative, or a definite integral, and interpret the mathematical result back in
      the original context.
\item \textbf{Evaluate limits and determine continuity} of algebraic, exponential,
      logarithmic, and trigonometric functions, including limits at infinity and limits
      that require the sandwich theorem.
\item \textbf{Differentiate} elementary, polynomial, rational, power, exponential,
      logarithmic, and trigonometric functions using the formal definition and the rules
      of differentiation (sum, product, quotient, chain, implicit).
\item \textbf{Apply derivatives} to find extrema, analyze monotonicity and concavity,
      solve optimization and related-rates problems, evaluate indeterminate forms
      (L'H\^{o}pital's Rule), and produce derivative-informed graphs.
\item \textbf{Evaluate definite and indefinite integrals}, state and apply both parts of
      the Fundamental Theorem of Calculus, and interpret a definite integral as
      cumulative change or an average value.
\item \textbf{Use technology} (graphing calculators or spreadsheets) to visualize
      functions and data, iterate recurrence equations, and implement simple numerical
      methods (bisection, Newton--Raphson).
\item \textbf{Communicate quantitative reasoning}, including the assumptions behind a
      mathematical model, its limitations, and how well it fits real or simulated data.
\end{enumerate}
